Modern.brandNameRationale: Anchor: Sicilian granita — the centuries-old semi-frozen ice tradition from Catania and Messina, the precursor to sorbet. 'Lab' frames the brand as a contemporary single-form studio: one form, many fruits, every batch logged.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern ice-cream brands are crowded with gelato and soft-serve operators; the granita form is editorially open. The opening is for a single-form ice brand that names the fruit, the sugar ratio, and the freezing time per batch.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Morgenstern's (morgensternsnyc.com) is the modern reference. Van Leeuwen (vanleeuwenicecream.com) holds the scaled-modern middle. OddFellows (oddfellowsnyc.com) plays the editorial peer. We sit alongside Morgenstern's with the granita form held narrowly.
Modern.positioningStatement: Granita Lab is a modern Sicilian-ice brand publishing the fruit, the sugar ratio, and the freeze time of every batch.

targetAudience.primary: Design-literate dessert buyers 26-45 who want a single form done seriously.
behaviors: Order the same flavour all summer
Care about sugar ratio and fruit source

dos: Name the fruit and the grower

Modern.logoDirection: Wordmark: GRANITA LAB set in a confident modern grotesk, two words on one line. Small mark: a single granita cup with a long spoon, used on cups and the batch ledger.

typography.primary: Söhne for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: Söhne Mono for sugar ratios and batch numbers
typography.rationale: A modern grotesk plus its mono — the batch-ledger register.

Modern.brandDescription: Granita Lab is a modern Sicilian-ice brand publishing the fruit, the sugar ratio, and the freeze time of every batch.
Modern.scope: Granita Lab works across the ice cream & gelato category with a single editorial register.
Modern.mission: Granita Lab is a modern Sicilian-ice brand publishing the fruit, the sugar ratio, and the freeze time of every batch.
Modern.vision: Granita Lab held in its register, indefinitely.

Luxury.tagline: A Paris ice room, by the bridge.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the Île Saint-Louis in Paris — the historic address that has stood for ice-cream excellence in the city since the mid-twentieth century. The address is geographic, not a live trademark; the brand inherits the prestige of place without leaning on a competitor's name.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury gelato is a small editorial category — single-shop houses on a known address, narrow flavours, no franchising. The opening is for a heritage Paris gelateria that holds the address as the brand.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Berthillon (berthillon.fr) plays the Paris reference. Grom (grom.it) holds the heritage Italian peer slot. Bachour (bachour.com) sits in the modern luxury middle. We sit as a Paris-address heritage house in the gelateria register.
Luxury.positioningStatement: Île Saint-Louis Gelateria is a Paris ice house holding a fixed catalog of nine flavours, served only from the shop on the bridge.

targetAudience.primary: Paris diners and seasonal visitors who treat the gelateria as a fixed summer ritual.
behaviors: Walk to the shop after dinner

dos: Name the bridge and the address
Print all signage in French and English

Luxury.logoDirection: Wordmark: ÎLE SAINT-LOUIS GELATERIA set in a classical book serif, three lines centered. Small mark: an embossed seal of the bridge silhouette, used on the cup lid.

typography.primary: Tiempos Headline for the wordmark and signage
typography.secondary: Garamond Premier Pro for body and the menu card
typography.rationale: A classical serif plus a reading serif — the heritage Paris register.

Luxury.brandDescription: Île Saint-Louis Gelateria is a Paris ice house holding a fixed catalog of nine flavours, served only from the shop on the bridge.

Luxury.mission: Île Saint-Louis Gelateria is a Paris ice house holding a fixed catalog of nine flavours, served only from the shop on the bridge.
Luxury.vision: Île Saint-Louis Gelateria held in its register, indefinitely.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the artisanal gelato cone — the single object that defines the take-away gelato format. One French word, accent retained. The diacritic is the only decoration the brand permits itself.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal gelato brands serve the design-literate dessert buyer — one form, one cone, one label.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most gelato brands lean folkloric or rainbow-palette. The minimal end is mostly empty. Morgenstern's (morgensternsnyc.com) is the closest editorial reference. We sit as the single-word minimal option.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Cône is a minimal gelateria selling one cone with three rotating flavours, served from a single window.

targetAudience.primary: Design-conscious dessert buyers 25-45 who want a small choice taken seriously.

Minimal.logoDirection: Wordmark: CÔNE set very large in a clean modern sans, four letters, accent retained. No symbol.

typography.primary: ABC Diatype for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: ABC Diatype Mono for the day's flavours
typography.rationale: Clean Diatype with its mono — the one-window register.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the Adriatic coast — the geographic spine of the Italian gelato tradition from Trieste to Bari. 'Cream Holdings' frames the brand as a multi-brand wholesale operator with a real heritage geography behind it.
Corporate.industrySummary: Wholesale gelato is consolidating under a small number of regional operators supplying hotels, restaurants, and grocery private-label. The opening is for a heritage-named operator with multi-line capacity.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Carpigiani (carpigiani.com) is the equipment-and-base reference. PreGel (pregel.com) holds the wholesale ingredient middle. MEC3 (mec3.com) plays the supplier peer. We sit as a wholesale finished-gelato operator with an Adriatic geographic anchor.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Adriatic Cream Holdings is a wholesale gelato operator supplying hotels, restaurants, and private-label clients across the Adriatic supply belt.

targetAudience.primary: Hotel F&B directors, restaurant procurement officers, and private-label brand managers.
behaviors: Renew on three to five-year terms

dos: Lead with production capacity and certifications
Refer to client brands by name in trade material
donts: No social media at the parent level

Corporate.logoDirection: Wordmark: ADRIATIC CREAM HOLDINGS set in an institutional serif, three lines. A small mark — a stylised wave above a scoop — used on contracts.

typography.primary: Tiempos Headline for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: Söhne for body and operational documents
typography.rationale: A reading serif plus a clean grotesk — the heritage wholesale register.

Creative.tagline: An ice for every kind of summer day.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the Sicilian habit of eating granita as a daily weather ritual — almond granita on hot mornings, coffee granita after lunch, lemon granita at four in the afternoon. The weather, not the menu, decides what's served.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative ice-cream brands play on ritual and narrative framing. Weather-as-menu is editorially rich and under-used outside Sicily.
Creative.competitorLandscape: OddFellows (oddfellowsnyc.com) is the editorial peer. Salt & Straw (saltandstraw.com) holds the seasonal-flavours middle. Morgenstern's (morgensternsnyc.com) is the modern reference. We sit as the weather-led creative brand.
Creative.positioningStatement: Granita Weather is a creative Sicilian-ice brand whose menu changes with the day's weather, not the season.

targetAudience.primary: City dessert buyers 25-45 who want a ritual, not a catalog.
behaviors: Check the forecast and the menu

dos: Post the day's forecast and the matching ice
Name the granita after the weather, not the fruit
Print the day's chalkboard on the shop window
donts: Open before the forecast is in

Creative.logoDirection: Wordmark: GRANITA WEATHER set in a warm display serif, two lines centered. Small mark: a single cloud above a granita cup, used on chalkboards and cups.

typography.primary: GT Sectra for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: Söhne for body and the forecast card
typography.rationale: A warm display serif plus a clean grotesk — the editorial weather register.

Creative.scope: Granita Weather works across the ice cream & gelato category with a single editorial register.
